concepts.label: te-node
concepts.gloss: A TE node is a network element or abstract switching vertex represented within a particular traffic-engineering topology.
concepts.example: R1 is a TE node in the OTN-layer topology and can host termination points for links toward R2, R3, and A1.
concepts.evidence: Kind `node`, `part-of` relation to `i.tetopo`, and instances R1–R3/A1–A3 indicate a topology vertex; ruled out `i.tp`, which is a link-facing termination located on a node.

concepts.label: termination-point
concepts.gloss: A termination point is a node-local endpoint at which a TE link terminates and through which the node attaches to that link.
concepts.example: `tp-R1-R2` is on R1 and terminates the R1–R2 TE link at the R1 end.
concepts.evidence: Kind `termination`, relations `on-node` and `terminates` a TE link, and instances such as `tp-R1-R2` identify a node-local link endpoint; ruled out `i.ttp`, which originates a tunnel rather than terminating a TE link.

concepts.label: supporting-tp
concepts.gloss: A supporting termination point identifies a server-layer termination that provides the underlying transport and adaptation support for another, client-layer termination point.
concepts.example: At R1, an optical-layer TP acts as the supporting TP for an OTN-layer TP carried over it.
instances: OTN tp over optical tp at R1
concepts.evidence: Kind `adaptation`, relation `supports` a termination point, and instance `OTN tp over optical tp at R1` indicate lower-layer support for a client-layer TP; ruled out `i.tp`, which is the supported endpoint itself rather than the support association.

concepts.label: tunnel-termination-point
concepts.gloss: A tunnel termination point is a node-local access endpoint from which a TE tunnel is originated into the TE topology.
concepts.example: `ttp-A1` is the tunnel head on node A1 from which the A1-to-A3 ODU2 tunnel originates.
concepts.evidence: Kind `termination`, relations `on-node` and `originates` a tunnel, plus tunnel-head instances at A1 and A3, identify a tunnel origination access point; ruled out `i.tcep`, which is an endpoint belonging to a tunnel connection rather than its originating node-local access point.

concepts.label: te-tunnel
concepts.gloss: A TE tunnel is an engineered transport service originating at a tunnel termination point and carried across a TE topology to provide constrained connectivity.
concepts.example: `tunnel-a1a3-odu2` carries an ODU2 service from the tunnel head at A1 across the OTN topology toward A3.
concepts.evidence: Kind `service`, relations `from` a tunnel termination point and `over` a TE topology, and the A1-to-A3 ODU2 instance indicate an engineered transport construct; ruled out `i.telink`, which is a topology adjacency rather than an end-to-end service.

concepts.label: otn-label
concepts.gloss: An OTN label is the tributary-slot and tributary-port-number allocation that identifies where a tunnel's ODU signal is multiplexed within a higher-rate OTN container.
concepts.example: For an ODU2 tunnel carried in an OTU4, the OTN label specifies the TS/TPN assigned to that ODU2 within the OTU4 payload.
concepts.evidence: Kind `multiplex`, relation `labels` a tunnel, synonyms `tributary-slot` and `TS/TPN`, and the ODU2-in-OTU4 instance indicate an OTN multiplex allocation; ruled out the tunnel itself, which is the carried service rather than its slot identifier.

concepts.label: connectivity-matrix
concepts.gloss: A connectivity matrix is a node-scoped representation of which termination points or interface groups can be internally connected by that node's switching function.
concepts.example: R2's connectivity matrix can state that traffic entering on its R1-facing TP may be switched to its R3-facing TP but not to an unsupported interface.
concepts.evidence: Kind `switching`, relation `on-node`, and instance `R2 connectivity matrix` indicate node-internal switching permissions; ruled out `i.tetopo`, which describes inter-node topology rather than allowable connectivity inside one node.

concepts.label: te-link
concepts.gloss: A TE link is a traffic-engineering adjacency between TE nodes whose ends are represented by termination points and whose resources can be used by routed connections or tunnels.
concepts.example: `telink-R1-R2` connects nodes R1 and R2 and is terminated by an R1-facing TP and a corresponding R2-facing TP.
concepts.evidence: Kind `link`, relations `between` TE nodes and `terminated-by` termination points, and instances such as `telink-R1-R2` identify a topology adjacency; ruled out `i.tunnel`, which is an engineered service carried over the topology.

concepts.label: te-topology
concepts.gloss: A TE topology is a layer-specific network graph that contains the TE nodes and TE links available for traffic-engineered path computation and resource use.
concepts.example: The OTN-layer topology contains nodes R1, R2, R3, A1, A2, and A3 together with links such as R1–R2 and R2–R3.
concepts.evidence: Kind `topology`, `contains` relations to TE nodes and TE links, synonym `per-layer network`, and instance `the OTN layer network` indicate a layer-specific TE graph; ruled out `i.tunnel`, which traverses this graph rather than containing it.

concepts.label: tunnel-connection-endpoint
concepts.gloss: A tunnel connection endpoint is a node-local endpoint belonging to a tunnel that terminates one of the tunnel's constituent connection segments at that node.
concepts.example: `tcep-a1a3-R1` represents the endpoint at R1 of a connection segment forming part of the A1-to-A3 tunnel, while `tcep-a1a3-R3` represents the corresponding tunnel connection endpoint at R3.
concepts.evidence: Kind `endpoint`, relations `on-node` and `part-of` a tunnel, and instances `tcep-a1a3-R1`/`tcep-a1a3-R3` identify node-resident endpoints of connections composing the tunnel; ruled out `i.ttp`, which is the access point that originates the tunnel.
